desc: E11 (m1n1-side, no kernel build): m1n1 always uses tag 0 -> NVMMU TCB slot 0; Linux draws from a pool with reserved_tags=2 so its I/O tag is NON-ZERO. This is one of only four remaining differences after E1-E10 matched nine properties and the fw still asserts. Force a non-zero tag in nvme_exec_command under a compile flag and re-run --wrap-march 200. If m1n1 then asserts at the wrap, the TCB slot index is the trigger and the Linux fix is to pin the I/O tag. Cheap: m1n1 build + chainload only. RESULT 2026-08-03: PASS with T6040_E11_TAG=2 (non-zero NVMMU TCB slot) — 200 reads / ~3 wraps, no assert. Transcript linux-build-out/e11-tag2-transcript.txt. The TCB slot index is NOT the trigger. Remaining diffs: (a) SQ doorbell window reg[3] vs reg[9] — Linux cannot be moved to reg[9] (E8 hang); (b) Identify + live depth-2 admin queue sharing the NVMMU (ticket 195); (c) real IRQ-context completion, which m1n1 cannot emulate (E9 only set the CQ flag; m1n1 never takes the MSI). (c) is now the strongest remaining candidate and is NOT testable from m1n1 — it needs either firmware RE (sol) or a Linux-side change that defers completion out of IRQ context.
